units.title: Settlement housing units advanced in the West Bank, by year
units.question: Housing units in settlement plans advanced by the Higher Planning Council (deposit or validation), West Bank excluding East Jerusalem. Advanced means a plan cleared a planning stage, not that homes were built.
units.note: Each year comes from a separate Peace Now report. 2026 is a partial year: the same Peace Now page gave 8,056 units to July 29, 2026. In 2025 some plans passed both stages and are counted once. Counting East Jerusalem, the EU's 2025 settlements report puts 2025 at 63,311 units

inss-approach.title: Israelis' preferred approach to the Israeli–Palestinian conflict, June 2026
inss-approach.question: Preferred approach to the Israeli–Palestinian conflict (INSS's summary of the options).

rows.label: Full annexation without granting civil rights

inss-approach.note: All respondents. The remaining answers, about 13%, went to other options INSS did not list in its summary; among Arab respondents 21% chose one binational state. Jews: separation 32%, annexation without civil rights 31%. Arabs: two states 57%. Coalition voters: annexation 50%. Opposition voters: separation 40%, two states 36%

pew-coexist.title: Israelis who think Israel and a Palestinian state can coexist peacefully
pew-coexist.question: "A way can be found for Israel and an independent Palestinian state to coexist peacefully." Share of all Israeli adults saying yes.
pew-coexist.note: Same question each year; 2013–2025 are from Pew's June 2025 report, 2026 from its September 2026 report. Jews: 16% in both 2025 and 2026. Arab respondents: 40% in 2025 and 23% in 2026, but 46% of Arab respondents gave no answer in 2026, so the drop is mostly non-response rather than a change of mind. In 2026, 56% of all respondents said it was not possible
